Meaning: To react to something.
Example: People respond to incentives.
Note: Core word in every elasticity definition.

Meaning: A limit on what you can do.
Example: Individuals make choices under constraints.

Meaning: Linked to each other.
Example: Choices made by consumers, firms and governments are interconnected.

Meaning: To meet or fulfil.
Example: We cannot satisfy every want.

Meaning: To share out among people.
Example: Equity is about how outcomes are distributed.

Meaning: To make separate parts work together.
Example: Separate decisions can coordinate economic activity.

Meaning: To appear gradually.
Example: Prices emerged and changed with scarcity.

Meaning: Both wanting to, and having the money to.
Example: How much consumers are willing and able to buy.
Note: Fixed phrase. It appears in EVERY definition of demand and supply.

Meaning: To keep unchanged while something else varies.
Example: Holding other things constant, price and quantity move in opposite directions.

Meaning: To cross each other.
Example: Equilibrium is where the two curves intersect.

Meaning: A force pushing something up or down.
Example: A shortage puts upward pressure on price.

Meaning: To change slightly to fit new conditions.
Example: Price adjustment moves the market back toward balance.

Meaning: How strongly something reacts.
Example: Elasticity measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded.

Meaning: Reacting strongly to.
Example: Elasticity tells us how sensitive demand is to price.

Meaning: The size of a number, ignoring its sign.
Example: We usually discuss the absolute value of elasticity.

Meaning: To make up for.
Example: The increase in sales compensates for the lower price.

Meaning: To cancel out.
Example: Quantity falls by just enough to offset the price rise.

Meaning: So small it is almost zero.
Example: At a single point, the change is infinitesimally small.

Meaning: A combination of goods taken together.
Example: Indifference analysis compares bundles of goods.

Meaning: Having no preference either way.
Example: The consumer is indifferent between any two points on the curve.
Note: NOT "not caring". It means equally happy with both.

Meaning: Touching a curve at exactly one point.
Example: The indifference curve is tangent to the budget line.

Meaning: To have enough money for.
Example: The budget line shows what the consumer can afford.

Meaning: To turn around a fixed point.
Example: A price change causes the budget line to rotate.
Note: Contrast with "shift", which moves the whole line.

Meaning: A move of the whole line, keeping the same slope.
Example: A change in income leads to a parallel shift.

Meaning: To change from one thing to another.
Example: Some consumers switch from coffee to tea.

Meaning: To work something out from something else.
Example: Plotting these combinations gives (derives) the demand curve.
Note: Very common instruction word in exams.

Meaning: What goes into production / what comes out.
Example: Labour and capital are inputs; wheat is the output.

Meaning: To make as large / as small as possible.
Example: The firm aims to maximise profit.

Meaning: For each single item.
Example: Average cost is total cost per unit of output.

Meaning: To begin and continue.
Example: Diminishing returns set in after point b.

Meaning: Rising sharply / rising gently.
Example: When the TPP curve is steep, marginal product is high.

Meaning: To divide across more units.
Example: Fixed cost is spread over more output, so AFC falls.

Meaning: General running costs not tied to one product.
Example: Economies of scope come from sharing overheads.

Meaning: Something that cannot be made smaller, so you need the whole thing.
Example: Indivisibilities are a source of economies of scale.

Meaning: Workers each doing one task very well.
Example: Specialisation of labour lowers unit costs.

Meaning: To make as effective as possible.
Example: Firms optimise their production processes.

Meaning: How strong competition is in a market.
Example: We classify markets by their degree of competition.

Meaning: To sort into groups.
Example: There are four main market structures.

Meaning: Controlled by a few large firms.
Example: The motor-vehicle industry is more concentrated.

Meaning: Exactly the same.
Example: Under perfect competition, products are identical.

Meaning: To discourage someone from doing something.
Example: A monopolist may deter entry by lowering price.

Meaning: To stop something happening.
Example: Patents prevent competitors from producing the same product.

Meaning: A competitor.
Example: An exclusive contract stops rivals reaching distributors.

Meaning: Absolutely necessary.
Example: A firm may control an essential input.

Meaning: To be close to, without being exactly.
Example: Agriculture approximates perfect competition.

Meaning: Good points / bad points.
Example: Advantages: production at minimum cost.
